title: Losing someone
hook: to Allah we belong and to Him we return (2:156)
tomorrow: after a funeral, what's actually useful?

segments.voice: Yesterday, with hardship: one line said twice, and the ease that comes inside the hard thing. Today, the hardest news, and the words for it.

A gentle note for parents: today is about a death. A text that just says: she passed, an hour ago. Thumbs hover. Every reply looks wrong. Sorry for your loss feels like a form letter, and anything longer feels like too much. What do you say in the first moment, before there's time to think? Muslims have words ready for exactly that moment, and they come straight from the Qur'an. A friend of another faith may arrive with words of her own, surprisingly close.
screen: `SHE PASSED, AN HOUR AGO.` → `EVERY REPLY LOOKS WRONG.` → `WORDS READY FOR THAT MOMENT.`

segments.voice: In Surah al-Baqarah, God says people will be tested with loss, of wealth and lives and the fruits of their work, and gives good news to the steadfast, who say, in Pickthall's words, when a misfortune strikes them: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." In Arabic: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. Two halves. We are Allah's: the person we lost was never ours to keep; they were His, and lent to us for a while. Unto Him we are returning: all of us, the one who died and the ones left at the graveside. It isn't only goodbye. It's a statement of where everyone is headed. The next verse says blessings and mercy from their Lord are on the people who say it. Now a neighbor. In the Hebrew Bible, read by Jews and Christians, Job loses everything, his children too, and says, in an older Jewish translation: "the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD." The old Book of Common Prayer reads it at Christian burials. What's shared: what we had was given, and not ours to hold forever. One honest difference: Job's line looks back, blessing God for both the giving and the taking. The ayah looks ahead, to where we're going: back to Him.
screen: `WE ARE ALLAH'S.` · `UNTO HIM WE ARE RETURNING.` · `JOB: THE LORD GAVE, AND HATH TAKEN.` · `ONE LOOKS BACK, ONE LOOKS AHEAD.` · then, large: `WE RETURN.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone you've lost, recently or long ago. Say their name, silently. If you pray, you can ask Allah's mercy and forgiveness for them, as Muslims do at a janazah; if not, hold their name, and a thank-you for the time you had.
Losing someone: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. We are Allah's, and to Him we are returning.
Hold onto this: we return, all of us, to the One who lent them to us. Go gently today.

screen: `DAY 1735 COUNTS.` → `HARD DAYS · 14 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: AFTER A FUNERAL, WHAT'S ACTUALLY USEFUL?`

howItsDone: On hearing of a death or any loss, Muslims say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un; the community washes and shrouds the body, prays the janazah prayer, buries quickly, and visits and feeds the bereaved family.
